name: Prompt Template & Variables
blurb: a prompt template with {{variables}} filled from a table or CSV, every rendered prompt previewed and missing values caught
intro: Renders a prompt template once per data row (CSV, TSV or a JSON array) with a small Mustache/Handlebars subset, and shows every rendered prompt with its token estimate, the values that are missing or empty, the columns never used and the rows over a token limit.

examples.title: Commit classifier over a TSV of commit messages

input.template:
Classify this commit message for the {{repo}} changelog.

<commit>
{{message}}
</commit>

Answer with one word: feat, fix, docs, refactor or chore.
input.data:
repo	message
firmware-dl200	sd: retry CMD25 once on timeout before failing the write
firmware-dl200	docs: describe the brown-out FAT sync in README
firmware-gw10	net: move net_rx watchdog kick into the socket poll loop

examples.title: Pin review from a JSON array with nested pin lists

usage: Give template (Mustache-like: {{x}}, {{x|default}}, {{#if}}/{{else}}, {{#unless}}, {{#each}} with {{.}} and {{@index}}), data (CSV/TSV with a header row, or a JSON array of objects), optionally mapping ("variable = column"), system (a system message), limit (tokens) and listSep. Returns the variables and the column each is bound to, per-row token estimates and status, findings (template syntax errors, variables no column provides, empty values per row, unused columns, rows over the limit), the rendered prompts as JSONL in chat messages format, and Python and JavaScript code equivalent to the template. Use it to build a batch or eval set from a spreadsheet, or to check a template before running it over data.
sources: mustache(5) - Logic-less templates, mustache.github.io/mustache.5.html (variables, sections, comments, standalone tags)
RFC 4180, Common Format and MIME Type for CSV Files
OpenAI Batch API / fine-tuning JSONL chat format ({"messages": [{"role", "content"}]}), platform.openai.com docs
Token estimate: chars/4 rule of thumb and a word-piece heuristic; not an exact tokenizer
